_comment: ADR-019 stage 19.3: the committed wall-clock baseline check_baseline.py compares fresh measure_baselines.py output against. Regenerate deliberately with `python -m backend.tests.perf.measure_baselines`, review the diff, and commit - never auto-overwritten by the nightly job itself (that would let a real regression quietly become the new normal).
measured_on: GitHub windows-latest - the nightly job's own runner - Python 3.12, coverage-uninstrumented. Each timing is the median of 7 publishes (measure_baselines.TIMING_REPEATS), and the value recorded is the SLOWEST of three workflow_dispatch runs of the same commit (runs 35464350837, 35464989364, 35464993252): runner-to-runner spread on one commit was up to 26% (stress.serialize_ms), so a baseline taken from one fast runner would fail the next slow one on noise. Sizes were identical across all three, as a deterministic metric should be.
